analysis: Examined the doc-only changes in docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump and the `stop` row describing per-request ReasoningStopScope), the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump, and EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift. In that file, an optional `stopStringScope: CBv2StopStringScope?` parameter (default nil) is threaded from runPump into pump. It is passed to matchedStopSequence(candidates:generatedTokens:scope:) at head line ~159, inside the `reason == .stop || .length` branch. Behavior: the matched-stop metadata replay now uses the request's scope. It affects only usage metadata recorded via usageSignal. It does not change decryption, encryption, authorization, attestation, prefix-cache storage, billing or resource release. The pump's terminal, teardown and retirement paths are untouched, so T-008 and T-041 mitigations are not changed. A nil scope keeps the earlier behavior. Remaining unverified items, which are outside the supplied source: (1) the submodule bump 7933a0f -> 7f00abc (libs/mlx-swift-lm) cannot be reviewed because its contents are not supplied, and it affects the inference engine (TB-007), so it needs a separate review; (2) the new `matchedStopSequence(... scope:)` overload in EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift and the callers that supply the scope were not shown, so I could not verify they compile or behave correctly. A mismatch there would affect only stop-sequence reporting accuracy, not confidentiality.
